what: The tenant cannot run a Power Automate inline-code action. This is the constraint that decides ITEM-18, and it is the only fact in this estate's record that did not come from the repository or from a command run against it.
classification: EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY — supplied by the operator, not derived from this repository.
statedBy: the repository owner, in session, 2026-09-03, answering the direct question 'can your tenant run a JavaScriptCode action?'
whyItWasAsked: Workflow Definition Language has no hash function and no bitwise operators, so SHA-256 cannot be computed in a flow expression. The only route inside Power Automate is an inline-code action, whose availability depends on the plan and the region. Nothing in this repository can establish whether a given tenant has it — the 58 exported definitions contain no inline-code action of any spelling, which shows it is unused here but not that it is unavailable.
howItIsRecorded: As a stated external fact, attributed and dated, not as a measurement. It is not reproducible from this repository and is not presented as though it were. If the tenant's plan changes, this record is what must be revisited.
consequence: INT-002's digest requirement cannot be met inside the upload flow, by any implementation, on this tenant. It is not a defect to be fixed, an unwritten action, or a porting job — it is a platform constraint. ITEM-18 moves from EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE to ACCEPTED on that basis.

whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.claim: The client computes a real SHA-256 and declares it per attachment.
whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.evidence: document-portal/js/submit.js:354 digestOf() uses crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …) over the file's ArrayBuffer and hex-encodes it; :447 declares one per attachment as sha256.
whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.caveat: crypto.subtle exists only in a secure context. digestOf returns the empty string when it is absent, and the declaration carries '' rather than failing, so an empty digest is possible and is not refused.

whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.evidence: docs/deployment/sharepoint/portal-field-spec.json declares DeclaredSha256 on Portal Attachments and on Portal Upload Tickets; the 2026-09-02 dry run reported both present in the tenant.

whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.claim: The size check is real and works.
whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.evidence: Portal_UPLOAD_ECM_DOCS compares DeclaredSizeBytes to Content-Length and answers 422 checksum-mismatch on a difference. That half of INT-002 is met.

whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.claim: The design's checksum action never ran and must not be ported.
whatWasVerifiedInTheRepositoryAlongsideI.evidence: Verify_Upload_Checksum in docs/deployment/power-automate-flows/02-portal-upload.flow.json is typed 'Javascript', which is not a Power Automate action type; its comparison target is an uninterpolated string literal, so a correct digest would be refused; and no inline-code action of any spelling appears in the 58 exported definitions.

compensatingControl.what: The digest is RECORDED, not ENFORCED.
compensatingControl.detail: A client-computed SHA-256 arrives with every attachment that has bytes and is stored as DeclaredSha256. It supports out-of-band verification later — an operator or a scheduled job outside Power Automate can re-hash the stored file and compare — but nothing verifies it at intake.
compensatingControl.whatItIsWorth: Against accidental corruption in transit it is useful, provided someone actually performs the later comparison. Against a caller who controls the client it is worth nothing, because that caller declares the digest as well as the bytes.
compensatingControl.whatItIsNot: It is not an integrity control at the boundary, and no document may describe it as one.

residualRisk: A file of the correct declared length whose contents differ from what the submitter intended is stored without objection. The size check still applies and still catches a length mismatch.
whatWouldReopenThis: A change to the tenant's Power Automate plan or region that makes an inline-code action available. At that point the action must be written from scratch — the design example is broken three ways and has never run — and demonstrated with two live uploads, one correct and one corrupted.
